NDT training in Lexington: how it works for Lexington employers and technicians

Short answer: Lexington employers and technicians get ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training from Atlantis NDT in two parts: live online theory, and hands-on practical sessions delivered onsite at the employer's facility under an ASNT Level III. Certification is employer-based, so the company's written practice defines the hours and experience, a Level III gives the exams, and the employer issues the certificate. Atlantis has no classroom building in Lexington; training is delivered online or at your site.

The Bluegrass region's inspection work is dominated by manufacturing rather than refining: automotive assembly and its tier-one supplier base, cranes and heavy equipment, defense aviation sustainment, and the power plants and pipelines that keep it all running. Manufacturing NDT runs on tight production schedules and customer quality audits, which is exactly where employer-site training pays off. Your technicians train on the parts, fixtures and procedures they will actually inspect, and the quality manager gets a file that matches the written practice line by line.

For recommended training hours and experience by method and level, use the NDT training requirements matrix. Your written practice may legitimately require more.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Lexington

All Atlantis courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A with content mapped to ANSI/ASNT CP-105. Each can run as live online theory, as an onsite course at a Lexington-area plant, or as a blend. The table shows how each method tends to be used across central Kentucky.

Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, IIFull-penetration weld inspection on structural and lifting equipment, spot-weld and bond checks in automotive, thickness surveys at plantsBasic maths for Level I; Level I plus OJT for Level II
Phased Array UT (PAUT)IIEncoded inspection of thick structural welds and production welds where traceable data is wantedUT Level II or equivalent

A typical central Kentucky manufacturer starts with MT, VT and UT, adds PT for aluminium and non-magnetic parts, and adds ET where aerospace or defense customers are involved. To map that to your plant, request a Lexington training quote.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Lexington, step by step

  1. Start with the written practice. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer. A Lexington supplier without a current written practice should fix that before training begins; see written practice development.
  2. Complete the formal training. Theory for the method and level, live online or onsite. Hours come from your written practice; recommended minimums are in the requirements matrix.
  3. Log on-the-job experience. Production inspection under a certified Level II or III, recorded session by session.
  4. General examination. Method principles, written, administered or approved by the Level III.
  5. Specific examination. Your equipment, your procedures and the acceptance criteria your customers impose, whether that is an automotive customer standard, AWS D1.1 or an aerospace specification.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on testing of specimens with known discontinuities, graded by a Level III. It is always in person.
  7. Vision test. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, normally repeated every year.
  8. Certification by the employer. Issued on the Level III's recommendation and filed for audit.
  9. Recertification. Intervals and criteria set in the written practice; diarise them so a customer audit does not find a lapsed certificate.

The full employer programme is described on SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Lexington crews

There is no Atlantis training centre in Lexington or elsewhere in Kentucky, and we will not pretend otherwise. Training reaches Lexington crews in three ways:

  • Live online. Instructor-led theory in real time, timed around first, second and third shifts. It covers the formal-training portion only. More on NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your plant. A Level III-led course at your facility in Lexington, Georgetown, Winchester, Richmond, Frankfort or wherever your line is, using your instruments and real production parts as practice specimens where appropriate.
  • Blended. Online theory first, then a short, concentrated practical block at your site. This suits suppliers who cannot release a whole team at once.

Manufacturing calendars drive the schedule. Model changeovers, planned shutdowns over holiday weeks and customer launch dates all affect when a crew can be released, and power plant outages pull contract technicians away in spring and autumn. We plan around those windows. Ask about onsite training for your Lexington crew and you will receive cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

Multi-plant suppliers can use corporate NDT training for one consolidated training plan, common records and Level III oversight across all their Kentucky and out-of-state sites.

Where NDT technicians work in Lexington

Within an hour of Lexington, NDT technicians find work in:

  • Automotive assembly and suppliers. Vehicle assembly in Georgetown and a dense ring of tier-one and tier-two suppliers across Scott, Madison, Mercer, Clark and Boyle counties. Typical NDT tasks include weld verification, casting and forging inspection, and supplier-quality audits where customers expect documented personnel qualification.
  • Cranes, lifting and heavy equipment. Crane and boom fabrication in Lexington relies on MT, UT and VT on high-strength structural welds, with AWS D1.1 and AWS D14 series welding codes common in this segment.
  • Defense aviation sustainment. Aircraft and equipment sustainment at Bluegrass Station uses PT, ET, MT and VT, usually under aerospace specifications in addition to SNT-TC-1A.
  • Power generation. Utility generating stations in central Kentucky, such as the E.W. Brown station near Harrodsburg, need boiler, piping and turbine inspection during planned outages.
  • Refining and petrochemicals. The large refinery at Catlettsburg in northeast Kentucky and chemical plants along the Ohio River in Louisville and Calvert City draw Lexington-based contractors for turnarounds, with ASME Section V, B31.3 and API code context.
  • Pipelines. Interstate natural gas and liquids pipelines cross Kentucky, and construction and integrity digs require RT and UT to API 1104.
  • Bridges and transport. The Kentucky Transportation Cabinet and its consultants inspect steel bridges statewide, including the large Ohio River crossings, where fracture-critical members call for VT, MT and UT.

Radiography licensing in Kentucky

Kentucky is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography licensing for radioactive materials is handled by the Radiation Health Branch of the Kentucky Cabinet for Health and Family Services, which also registers radiation-producing machines such as industrial X-ray units. A Lexington RT company holds the state licence; its radiographers and radiographer's assistants must meet the training and certification requirements in Kentucky's radiation rules, which follow the NRC industrial radiography framework, including radiation safety training, recognised radiographer certification, personal monitoring, calibrated survey instruments and the two-person rule at temporary job sites. Crews from other states usually need reciprocity before working in Kentucky.

Atlantis RT courses teach technique, exposure calculation, film and digital interpretation and radiation safety principles for SNT-TC-1A certification. They do not grant authority to use sources; that comes from the licensee and the state.

Method spotlight: magnetic particle testing on cranes and heavy equipment

Central Kentucky builds and maintains a lot of heavily loaded welded steel, from crane booms and outriggers to vehicle frames, axles and suspension parts. For ferromagnetic steel with fatigue-loaded welds, magnetic particle testing is the workhorse surface method, and it is the method most Lexington manufacturers ask about first.

An MT Level II course for this market goes beyond the basics of yokes and powders. It typically covers:

  • Choosing between yoke, prod, coil and head-shot magnetisation, and why prods are often restricted on finished or high-strength parts.
  • Field direction and the need for two perpendicular inspections to find cracks in any orientation, especially at weld toes and gussets.
  • Wet fluorescent versus visible dry powder, UV-A intensity and white-light limits, and how to verify them.
  • Field-strength verification with shims or pie gauges, and demagnetisation where machining or welding follows.
  • Interpreting relevant, non-relevant and false indications, and applying the acceptance criteria in AWS D1.1, AWS D14 series codes or the customer's standard.

MT pairs naturally with UT for subsurface volumetric checks on full-penetration welds, which is why many central Kentucky technicians certify in both. For UT exam preparation, see UT Level 2 practice questions.

Level III services and written practices for Lexington NDT companies

A trained technician still needs a compliant programme around them. For Lexington manufacturers, suppliers and inspection firms we offer:

  • Written practice creation or revision to SNT-TC-1A, including the 2024 edition changes; see written practice development.
  • Exam administration by a Level III for general, specific and practical exams, with records your customer's supplier-quality auditor can follow.
  • Procedure and technique sheets written or reviewed against the code or customer specification you inspect to.
  • Level III of record for suppliers who need Level III authority without a full-time hire.

For consulting rather than courses, our nearest Kentucky consulting page is steel NDT Level III consulting in Frankfort, Kentucky, a short drive from Lexington. The statewide view, with every Kentucky city we cover, is on NDT training in Kentucky. Book a Level III consultation if you would rather talk through your programme first.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT simulator gives trainees time on 12 NDT methods across 5 3D environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Between theory and the practical block, it is a low-risk way to rehearse set-ups, scanning patterns and indication interpretation. The Practical NDT page for Lexington explains how local trainees use it.

It is practice, not certification. The simulator does not count as OJT and does not replace the practical exam on real specimens graded by a Level III.

Your instructor

Courses are led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He is responsible for course content, practical sessions and examinations, and he works directly with employers on written practices and certification records.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Lexington

How do I get NDT certified in Lexington, KY?

Complete formal training in a method, gain documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams given or approved by a Level III, pass a vision test, and be certified by your employer under its written practice. That is the ASNT SNT-TC-1A route used across US manufacturing. Atlantis supplies the training and can support the exams and written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Kentucky?

Theory, yes. Live online classes cover the formal-training requirement. Practical training and the practical exam must be done in person, onsite at your employer or at an arranged location. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the written practice, whether you already hold UT Level I and how fast you can accumulate documented experience. SNT-TC-1A sets recommended minimum training and experience, and employers may set more. The recommended figures are in the training requirements matrix. Expect the experience requirement to take longer than the classroom part.

Do I need a licence for industrial radiography in Kentucky?

Your employer needs a radioactive-materials licence from the Kentucky Radiation Health Branch, and you must meet the state's radiographer or assistant training and certification rules before working with sources. NDT method training is necessary but not sufficient.

What does NDT training cost in Lexington?

Cost depends on methods, levels, number of trainees, the delivery format and whether you need exams or written-practice work as well, so we quote each request. Request a Lexington training quote and we will send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Lexington employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the standard reference for NDT personnel qualification across US manufacturing, power and construction, and many customer specifications build on it. Aerospace and defense customers may add their own requirements. Certification is employer-specific, so a new employer will recertify you, but your training and experience records travel with you.

Can you train our team at our plant in Georgetown or Winchester?

Yes. Onsite delivery anywhere in the Lexington region is standard for employer cohorts. We work around your production schedule and use your own equipment and procedures where they are suitable.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA to pay for NDT training?

Only at approved providers. GI Bill benefits require a programme approved for VA education benefits, and WIOA training funds generally require a provider on the state's Eligible Training Provider List, which Kentucky administers through the Kentucky Career Center network. Atlantis does not hold or claim either approval. Most technicians who train with us are sponsored by their employer or prospective employer; if you want to use education benefits, an approved college programme is the better route.

Which NDT method is most useful in central Kentucky?

MT, VT and UT cover most manufacturing and structural work. PT and ET open doors in aerospace and defense sustainment; RT is useful for pipeline, power and pressure-vessel work. See the NDT salary guide for how level and method affect pay.

We are an automotive supplier. Do we need SNT-TC-1A?

Not every automotive customer requires it, but when a customer specification calls for qualified NDT personnel, SNT-TC-1A is the usual US reference, and having a written practice gives your audit trail a clear structure. We can review your customer requirements and tell you what is actually needed.

Do you train for API, CWI or ISO 9712 certifications?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Kentucky employers also ask for AWS CWI for welding inspection or API credentials at refineries; those are separate schemes. We can explain how they sit alongside SNT-TC-1A certification.

Can Atlantis prepare me for ASNT Level III?

Yes. Preparation covers the Basic exam, method exams and the practical knowledge of writing procedures and administering exams. See ASNT Level III training.
